questions.title: Which month of 2026 will have the highest ICE arrest total in the data publicly available by August 26, 2026?
questions.background: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) carries out arrests as part of federal immigration enforcement.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Use government data supplied by ICE, as reported by The Associated Press. Resolution Date : Resolve to the calendar month of 2026 with the largest arrest total among the months covered by the latest ICE monthly figures publicly available by August 26, 2026. Accepted Answer Format : Answer with the month name only.
questions.current_reasoning: Two major July 15-19 developments materially reshape the distribution, lifting both January and July while squeezing June: (1) Severe ICE data blackout (The Marshall Project, July 15; Texas Tribune, July 10): ICE has NOT published its statutory semimonthly Detention Management report on arrests, detentions, and deportations since April 9—over three months dark—and has refused media/academic requests amid three lawsuits (blaming government shutdowns, though saying it is working to release the report), while UC Berkeley's Deportation Data Project FOIA dataset analyzed by AP still ends March 11, 2026 (and DHS publicly disputed DDP on July 10). This substantially raises the risk (~35-42%) that June/July monthly figures are not yet publicly available by August 26, reinforcing January (~38k-39k high-water mark before the post-Minneapolis drop) as the clear #1 (0.48 -> 0.54); (2) Swift reversal of the ICE vehicle-stop pause (CBS News, Korea Herald, Hindustan Times, July 16 & 19): less than 24 hours after DHS Secretary Mullin paused most vehicle stops following the Houston and Maine fatal shootings, President Trump publicly overruled the pause on July 16 and reinstated vehicle stops (defended by Border Czar Tom Homan on Face the Nation July 19). Because July now runs a full 31 days under Trump's late-June 2,000/day surge order (unlike June, which surged only in its final week), July is strongly favored over June whenever summer figures are published by August 26—lifting July 0.21 -> 0.24 ahead of June (trimmed 0.24 -> 0.17), with May 0.02 and March 0.01 (2% residual for Feb/Apr/Aug).

questions.background: António Guterres is serving as UN secretary-general. Informal Security Council straw polls gauge support for potential successors, with members indicating whether they encourage, discourage or have no opinion on each candidate.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official UN information or contemporaneous reporting by reputable international news organizations describing the first Security Council straw poll in the 2026 secretary-general selection process. Resolution Condition : Resolve to the candidate receiving the highest number of “encourage” votes in that first poll, regardless of subsequent polls or the final appointment. Accepted Answer Format : The candidate’s full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Key 2026-07-20/21 development right ahead of the first UNSC straw poll (reported by The EastAfrican on July 16 as scheduled to start around July 23, with final candidate hearings wrapping up late July): Senegalese President Bassirou Diomaye Faye formally endorsed former President Macky Sall after meeting him July 17 and instructed his government to 'fully mobilize' diplomatic backing ('Senegal's candidacy in the service of Africa', Reuters/Straits Times July 20-21). Removing Sall's home-country handicap materially boosts his approval-poll upside with the three African UNSC members (including July Council President DRC, plus Somalia and Liberia), France, and Global South delegates, lifting Sall 0.03 -> 0.09. Separately, Anadolu Agency (July 10) confirmed UNSC completed informal dialogues with Sall (July 7), Rafael Grossi (July 7), and Guyana's Carolyn Rodrigues-Birkett (July 9, a 2024-25 UNSC colleague), while María Fernanda Espinosa's hearing was pushed to July 27; placing Rodrigues-Birkett into the 5th slot at 0.03 (leaving 0.03 residual mainly for Espinosa). Frontrunners Rebeca Grynspan (0.42 -> 0.40) and Rafael Grossi (0.41 -> 0.39) remain in a virtual dead heat, with Michelle Bachelet trimmed 0.07 -> 0.06.

questions.title: Which international organization, if any, will first gain direct access to Aung San Suu Kyi in detention during 2026?
questions.background: Aung San Suu Kyi has been detained since Myanmar's military overthrew her government in February 2021. Her access to outside visitors has been tightly restricted.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Public statements from the visiting organization or Myanmar authorities, corroborated by established news reporting. Qualifying Event : Direct access means a completed in-person meeting with Suu Kyi by a representative acting on behalf of an international organization. Permission or an announced plan without a completed visit does not qualify. Resolution : Resolve to the first international organization publicly confirmed to have completed such a visit during 2026. If no qualifying visit is confirmed by December 31, 2026, resolve that no organization qualified. Accepted Answer Format : The organization's name, or a statement that no organization qualified.
